title: Chesterton - The Honour Of Israel Gow

evidence.paraphrase: The investigators catalogue an inventory of unexplained objects found in the castle to be examined.
evidence.quote: I will read the inventory," began Craven gravely, picking up one of the papers, "the inventory of what we found loose and unexplained in the castle.

evidence.paraphrase: The central puzzle is framed as the challenge of finding a connection among the disparate items.
evidence.quote:
By no stretch of fancy can
      the human mind connect together snuff and diamonds and wax and loose
      clockwork.

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown distinguishes between plausible false explanations and the single real explanation being sought.
evidence.quote:
Ten false philosophies
      will fit the universe; ten false theories will fit Glengyle Castle. But we
      want the real explanation of the castle and the universe.

evidence.paraphrase: Flambeau expresses fear about what will be found in the grave.
evidence.quote: "I am afraid of finding it," said Flambeau.

evidence.paraphrase: Craven reacts with shock upon discovering the corpse has no head.
evidence.quote: "God!" cried the man by the coffin, "but he hasn\u2019t got a head."

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown reacts with startled self-reproach at suddenly grasping the solution.
evidence.quote:
Father Brown\u2019s pipe fell out of his mouth and broke into three pieces on
      the gravel path. He stood rolling his eyes, the exact picture of an idiot.
      "Lord, what a turnip I am!"

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown offers a technical explanation linking diamonds and steel wheels to glass-cutting tools.
evidence.quote:
Diamonds and small steel wheels are the only two instruments
      with which you can cut out a pane of glass.

evidence.paraphrase: The final explanation reveals every strange item is what remains after all gold parts were removed.
The apparent crime is reframed as an act of scrupulous, literal honesty rather than theft.
evidence.quote:
This is not a story of crime," he said; "rather it is the story of a
      strange and crooked honesty. We are dealing with the one man on earth,
      perhaps, who has taken no more than his due.

evidence.paraphrase: The backstory explains the earl's obsession and his decision to make the deaf servant his heir.
evidence.quote:
He swore he was Diogenes, that had long sought an honest man,
      and at last had found one. He made a new will, which I have seen.

evidence.paraphrase: The final detail explains the missing head as motivated by removing a gold tooth.
evidence.quote:
He will put the skull back in the grave, when he
      has taken the gold out of the tooth.

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown deduces from the gardener's methodical digging pattern that something is hidden in one spot.
evidence.quote: There must be a mighty fine potato just here.
